claim: A blocking resume of an agent that is still running - Agent({resume:<id>, run_in_background:false}) - is not refused. It returns pi's internal error text, flips the live agent's record to status error (hasRunning() goes false, steer_subagent refuses, stop/abortAll skip it), and a follow-up get_subagent_result marks it consumed, so the real answer that lands seconds later is never notified. The default (background) resume path guards exactly this case; the foreground path does not.
evidence: cmd: cd probes/agents && ./RUN.sh p05-resume-and-mention.probe.test.ts -t R1 -> out/p05-r1-blocking-resume-of-running-agent.json: reply `Agent failed: Agent is already processing. Specify streamingBehavior ('steer' or 'followUp') to queue the message.` (isError:false); record right after, original run still in flight: {status:"error", completedAt:true}, manager.hasRunning()=false; steer_subagent -> `Agent "…" is not running (status: error). Cannot steer a non-running agent.`; get_subagent_result -> `Status: error … Error: Agent is already processing…`; 3.5 s later the record is {status:"completed", result:"CHILD_FINAL_ANSWER", error:<stale text>, resultConsumed:true} and the parent received zero subagent-notification messages. Code: the running/queued refusal exists only inside `if (runInBackground)` src/index.ts:2132-2144; the foreground branch calls manager.resume directly src/index.ts:2168 -> src/agent-manager.ts:1190-1231; abort()/abortAll() act only on status running src/agent-manager.ts:1442, :1543. SUPPORTED, not reproduced: the failed resume also aborts the live run's nested children (src/agent-manager.ts:1229) and the nested Agent tool has the same unguarded call (src/nested-tools.ts:189). Guarded contrast: out/p13-background-resume-refusal.json.
cost: Orchestrating LLM and operator. Backgrounds are the default, so the agent a model wants to 'resume and wait for' is usually still running; each such call leaves a live run that cannot be steered or stopped and whose result can be lost.
cureHint: Hoist the running/queued refusal (src/index.ts:2139-2144) above the runInBackground branch and make AgentManager.resume() refuse running/queued records on the foreground path too (covers the nested tool).

No-root call in a workspace with no src (the scratch rf workspace): ok:true, rows 1 (kinds ['hx.fs/namespace']), execution_status.kind 'incomplete', diagnostic '.../rf-ws/src names no entry (trace outcome Missing, existence Unknown)' (probes/providers/h02-hx-nosrc.json). Code: src/workbench/providers/hyperunix.ts:50 (`root??"src"`), :14. The injected-reader registration (:16-27) applies no default, so the two registrations of one id differ.
cost: Agents on any repository that is not laid out as src/ (monorepos, Python, Go): a plausible call returns a confusing non-answer; every agent must discover the kind vocabulary by failing.
cureHint: Add description, examples (hx.fs/regular-file) and default to the schema properties; require root explicitly or state the default in the contract; point at `hx schema list` for kinds.

claim: Authorization refusals never name the missing grant, and the Claude-role journey needs three separate grants per capability (discover:<id>, invoke:<id> and the producer permission) on top of role exposure. With any one missing the agent sees 'Claude capability permission denied.' or an empty discover list, indistinguishable from 'nothing is installed'. The same producer grant that makes node() work leaves the Claude tools fully denied.
evidence: Role capabilities ['hyperunix.find'] over a real MCP client (probes/providers/h03-run-grants.out): grants ['hyperunix:read'] -> discover {capabilities:[]}, contract and invoke 'Claude capability permission denied.'; ['hyperunix:read','invoke:hyperunix.find'] -> discover [] and contract denied, invoke works; ['invoke:hyperunix.find'] -> invoke 'Permission denied for capability hyperunix.find (invoke).'; ['discover:hyperunix.find'] -> discover and contract work, invoke denied. node() with ['hyperunix:read'] alone succeeds (probes/providers/vt/node-e2e.log s1) and without it reports 'Permission denied for capability hyperunix.find (invoke).' (s5). Unknown id through the Claude tool -> 'Claude capability permission denied.' rather than unknown capability (probes/providers/h03-run2.out). Contrast: src/workbench/claude-evidence.ts:89 names its grant. Docs: one sentence at docs/workflows.md:464; no shipped .pi/subagents.json example pairs roles.<name>.capabilities with the three grants (grep of README.md, docs/workflows.md, docs/workbench/*.md).
cost: Operators wiring a Claude role to a provider: trial and error over three grant strings with an identical denial each time; agents handed the tools with a missing discover grant hit an empty list and stop.
cureHint: Name the missing grant in the refusal (the operator already owns the grant list), and ship one worked settings block in docs/workbench/19.

claim: A missing producer binary surfaces four different ways across the four providers, and nothing warns before invocation: three use category transport and one unavailable; only Furnace says ENOENT; Forge reports a closed connection; RF does not name rf. Discovery still lists all four capabilities, the extension has no preflight or doctor surface, and the shipped docs say only 'Install those executables independently'.

Same PATH, capability_discover still returns all four (probes/providers/h03-run-nobin-discover.out). Absence surfaces: grep of src for doctor|healthcheck -> 0 hits (probes/providers/census.out; the one 'preflight' in src is furnace-hosted contract decoding); vendor/README.md:3 is the only install statement; no minimum versions anywhere in README.md, docs/workflows.md, docs/workbench/17.

cureHint: Use category unavailable with one sentence shape ('<tool> executable not found on PATH') in all four providers, and add a preflight (settings menu row or a workbench doctor reply) that reports each binary's presence and version.

claim: The registry's default 30 s deadline fires before the RF provider's own 60 s bound, so that bound and its 'RF preview exceeded the execution deadline.' message are unreachable under the host's registry (reproduced). By code read only (SUPPORTED, not run): hyperunix.find's 30 s wall bound with a 60 s SDK timeout races the same 30 s cut, so a slow query would be reported as a registry timeout instead of HX's bounded partial answer.

Code: src/workbench/capability-registry.ts:62 (CAPABILITY_DEADLINE_MS 30_000), src/index.ts:2490 (new CapabilityRegistry() with no limits), src/workbench/providers/reactivefiber.ts:157,174 (60_000), src/workbench/providers/hyperunix.ts:21,42 (wall '30s', timeoutMs 60_000). Code: src/workbench/providers/forge.ts:114-161 (spawn, initialize, request, close per call). For scale: rf preview 2.5-3.4 s per call, hx find 0.25-0.45 s.

claim: On a dolt-backed RF workspace the 'read' preview capability starts a persistent rf-owned dolt sql-server (about 103 MB resident, with a listening port) that outlives the call. Second reproduction: an earlier run in this session measured rss_bytes 103882752. The port's bind address was not examined. The provider promise settled, so no admission slot leaks. Docs: grep -i dolt over README.md, docs/workflows.md, docs/workbench/*.md finds only the Beads ledger sentence; closed bead wb-pfxo.8 pins reclamation as an absent-today leg.

Timeout duration was set to 1.' and 31 manager.spawn calls within 60 ms; addJob('+30d') -> spawn after ~1 ms, job auto-disabled; detectSchedule('+99999999999d') throws 'RangeError: Invalid time value'. claim: ScheduleStore's PID lock is acquired with a synchronous busy-wait (up to 100 x 50 ms) that starves the event loop: with a lock held by a live pid every mutation freezes the TUI for ~5 s and then throws.

Code: src/schedule-store.ts:38-40 `while (Date.now() - start < LOCK_RETRY_MS) { /* busy wait */ }`, :17-18 LOCK_RETRY_MS=50, LOCK_MAX_RETRIES=100. README.md:102 advertises 'PID-based file locking for cross-instance safety'.
cost: Two pi instances on one cwd/session (or a crashed pi whose pid was reused) turn every schedule add/update/fire into a 5-second UI hang on the main thread; fires inside setInterval callbacks also block.
cureHint: Make the store async (await setTimeout between retries) or use an O_EXCL open with a short bounded retry; the files are per-session so contention is rare — a 250 ms total bound would do.
